Overall the attacks can be tanked by players with good defense, but are also relatively easy to avoid.

moves.severity: moderate, more on return, can shotgun

Can be tanked by builds with good defenses, but are also pretty easy to avoid.

moves.name: Earthquake
moves.tell: fires out a tremor in a line towards the player
moves.avoid: Keep moving to make it easier to avoid Earthquake.
moves.maxrollQuote: Abomination fires out a tremor in a line towards the player. Upon reaching its destination (the place you were standing when the skill was used) it erupts into a small earthquake that deals moderate Physical Damage. Once the Abomination is below 90% health, this attack also casts Spirit Decay.

moves.name: Spirit Decay
moves.tell: Once the boss reaches 90%, be on the lookout for the Necrotic AoE circles from Spirit Decay.
moves.avoid: These slowly chase you and ramp up their damage, so they need to be avoided.

tips: Spirit Decay circles chase you and ramp up their Necrotic damage after he drops below 90 percent. Keep moving so they trail behind you and never stand still in one.
Necrotic Wave returns to him for more damage and can hit several times. Stand between two waves at range, or get behind him before they come back.
When the red Tail Flare circle appears, move to his side so you clear both the circle and the Fire lines that can Ignite.
strategy: Phase 1: In phase 1, he is invulnerable until you destroy four Vessels. Run to the center area to activate the boss and start the fight, then immediately run to one of the Vessels. Try to take it out in one shot if possible.... As you destroy vessels, Necrotic pools form in each quarter of the arena that the vessel was positioned in. Go in a clockwise or counter clockwise pattern until all four Vessels are killed, which helps you avoid the Necrotic pools when switching between vessels. Once all four Vessels are destroyed, immediately head to the center ring.
Phase 2: Once you've destroyed all four Vessels and reached the center ring, you can start damaging the boss.

Torch Flame, Magma Ball and the third Lava Plume explosion hit hardest. Avoid those first and absorb the rest with defenses.
Damage is almost all Fire and Necrotic. Cap both resistances and group the Shamans for area damage when they stand close.
strategy: Single phase: Bhuldar, Herkir, and Logi is a single phase fight. The Shamans have most of their abilities from the beginning, but the fight gets significantly harder when a Shaman dies.

Maxroll guide line: Try to group them up and AoE them down. The Shamans have separate health pools so hitting them all at once effectively cuts the fight time down by 2/3rds vs. hitting them one at a time.
Maxroll guide line: It's almost impossible to avoid all of the attacks so the fight is largely about prioritizing mechanics and having sufficient defenses to deal with the rest.
Maxroll guide line: This is especially challenging for Melee builds because the other Shamans can stand in the Necrotic pool while using their own skills, making it difficult to reach them.
Maxroll guide line: Kill the Shamans at the same time to avoid dealing with Spirit Form.
volcanic-shaman.resist: Damage is almost exclusively Fire and Necrotic, so make sure to cap both Resistances.
extra_claims: Identity note: Maxroll names the Spirits of Fire boss "Bhuldar, Herkir, and Logi (AKA The Shamans)", three bosses with separate health pools. The catalog display name Volcanic Shaman comes from the Tunklab preview. No alias was added; killer strings need in-game capture.

page.title: Emperor of Corpses – Reign of Dragons Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL

moves.name: Soul Bomb
moves.severity: high; kills most builds caught in it
moves.tell: immediately leave the area as soon as Emperor rears up on his hind legs.
moves.avoid: Make sure you're far enough away from the outer circle to not get clipped. As soon as the explosion occurs, run back in to avoid the DoT that forms. Make sure to keep Emperor towards the center of the arena or you could end up without enough room to run out of the circle.
moves.maxrollQuote: Emperor rears up onto his hind legs and fires his breath into the ground, creating a very large circle. After a short period the circle explodes dealing high Necrotic Damage that kills most builds caught in it. After the explosion, the area outside of the circle deals a Necrotic DoT that becomes stronger over time.

moves.name: Roar
moves.avoid: It's not a dangerous attack on its own, but if he uses just before Soul Bomb the Slow stacks can make it very difficult to avoid the explosion.
moves.maxrollQuote: Emperor roars, slowing the player and summoning 5 Slaughtered Thralls which deal low Physical Damage and have a small Health pool. He gains this skill once he reaches 70% HP.
moves.note: Roar itself slows; the 5 Slaughtered Thralls it summons deal low Physical damage (element kept off Roar)

moves.name: Flesh Impact
moves.avoid: Try to avoid getting hit by several in a short period of time.
moves.maxrollQuote: Emperor shakes and fires out pieces of his own body that explode on impact, dealing moderate Necrotic Damage and spawning a Slaughtered Thrall.

moves.name: Spirit Breath
moves.severity: high DoT; kills most builds caught for over a second
moves.tell: Look for Emperor to raise his head up.
moves.avoid: When he does, move to his side or his back to avoid the attack.
moves.maxrollQuote: Emperor raises his head high and then breathes out a high damage Necrotic DoT in a conal pattern that becomes more powerful over time. This kills most builds caught in it for longer than a second.

moves.name: Blood Pools
moves.severity: Since the damage they do is always a fraction of existing health they cannot kill you outright
moves.avoid: Try to stay in the center of the arena and escape Soul Bomb by running to the bottom where no Blood Pools form.
moves.maxrollQuote: Throughout the fight Blood Pools spawn on the edges of the arena. These pools have no damage type, instead damaging a large percentage of existing health every second. Since the damage they do is always a fraction of existing health they cannot kill you outright, but they reduce health at an alarming rate and leave players vulnerable to other attacks.
moves.note: Maxroll: "These pools have no damage type"

moves.name: Melee Attack
moves.avoid: This ability can be tanked.
moves.maxrollQuote: Emperor swipes with his front leg dealing low Physical Damage to players in Melee Range. This ability can be tanked.

tips: Soul Bomb kills most builds inside it. When he rears up, run clear of the circle, then step back in after the blast to avoid the outer Necrotic damage.
Spirit Breath is a ramping Necrotic cone. When he raises his head, move to his side or back.
Blood Pools at the edges take a share of current health each second. Keep him near the center and escape Soul Bomb toward the bottom where pools do not form.
strategy: Single phase: Emperor is a single phase fight and he has nearly all of his skills from the start. The only skill he doesn't start with is activated at 70% HP, so most of the fight involves Emperor's entire toolkit. However, the arena does get more challenging over time as Blood Pools are formed throughout the fight.
Maxroll guide line: This fight is mainly about positioning and timing to avoid Soul Bomb and Spirit Breath. Get those down and Emperor becomes a much easier fight.
Maxroll guide line: Soul Bomb is the his most dangerous mechanics. Avoid it at all costs.
emperor-of-corpses.resist: Damage is mostly Necrotic with some Physical, so cap these Resistances.

page.title: Formosus the Undying – Blood, Frost, and Death Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL

moves.name: Teleport
moves.avoid: When Formosus Teleports he often moves off screen. Be prepared to search for him.
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus teleports to a new location. He can teleport to anywhere in the arena which means he often teleports to somewhere off screen. Teleport does no damage.
moves.note: Maxroll: "Teleport does no damage"

moves.name: Ice Patch
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus places a large patch of ice on the ground that Slows. It does no damage.
moves.note: Maxroll: "It does no damage"

moves.name: Undead Wengari
moves.avoid: Killing the Axe Throwers and the Matriarch forces Formosus to choose only one to Resurrect, giving you a much better chance of not having to deal with the Matriarch for long stretches of the fight.
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus is accompanied by three Undead Wengari Axe Throwers and an Undead Wengari Matriarch. The axe throwers have a projectile that deals low Physical Damage. The Matriarch has a Melee Attack and a Leap Attack that causes an Earthquake with an Aftershock. Both deal Primarily Lightning Damage but the Earthquake is far more deadly.
moves.note: Axe Throwers: low Physical projectile. Matriarch melee and Leap earthquake: primarily Lightning

moves.name: Resurrect Wengari
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus resurrects one Undead Wengari that has been slain in combat.

moves.name: Spirit Beam
moves.avoid: Spirit Beam deals a lot of damage but is easy to avoid. If there is an Ice Patch on the ground it becomes significantly harder. Having a movement ability makes it much easier to deal with these overlapping mechanics.
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus channels a large beam in front of him for several seconds that deals high Necrotic Damage and gets stronger over time.

moves.name: Frost Spirit
moves.avoid: Frost Spirit does low damage and can be tanked. The homing aspect of the skill makes it difficult to dodge so focus on other mechanics and use a potion if you need to.
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus fires several projectiles that seek out the player and deal low Cold and Necrotic Damage

moves.name: Ice Vortex
moves.severity: The damage from Ice Vortex ramps up over time and becomes deadly.
moves.avoid: Make sure to account for where these are at all times and stay out of them. They start off with low damage so if Formosus places one on top of you there's enough time to move out before it starts to hurt.
moves.maxrollQuote: Formosus places several tornado-like DoTs on the ground that slowly move in random directions and deal Cold Damage that gets stronger over time.

tips: Spirit Beam deals high Necrotic damage and gets harder to dodge on an Ice Patch. Keep a movement skill ready to leave the beam.
Ice Vortex ramps up and becomes deadly. Track every vortex and step out early while the damage is still low.
The Wengari Matriarch's fast Leap Slam earthquake deals mostly Lightning. Kill her when you can and cap Cold, Necrotic and Lightning resistance.
strategy: Single phase: Formosus is a single phase fight. He has all of his abilities from the start, meaning this fight does not get more challenging over time. Formosus also has four Undead Wengari (three Axe Throwers and one Matriarch) that fight with him and can be resurrected if they fall in battle.

Maxroll guide line: Overall, there's a lot of moving parts to this fight but most of them don't matter. What does matter is Spirit Beam, Ice Vortex and Leap Slam. If you can avoid those three attacks you will kill Formosus.
Maxroll guide line: The Axe Throwers aren't dangerous, but the Matriarch is.
Maxroll guide line: Having a movement ability in case you get stuck in Spirit Decay with an Ice Patch is a good idea.
frost-lich-formosus.resist: Damage is mostly Cold and Necrotic, with the Wengari dealing mostly Lightning Damage, so cap all three of these Resistances.
extra_claims: Identity note: Maxroll titles this guide "Formosus the Undying"; the catalog keeps Frost Lich Formosus as the display name per prior research.

page.title: God Hunter Argentus – The Stolen Lance Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Turrets
moves.tell: They target where the player is standing and follow for a short period before locking onto a location. The telegraph is easy to see
moves.avoid: Avoid Turret projectiles by strafing when the telegraph starts and continuing to do so until they lock in.
moves.maxrollQuote: Three Turrets Fire a Projectile at the player from outside of the arena. They target where the player is standing and follow for a short period before locking onto a location. The telegraph is easy to see and can be avoided by strafing until the Turrets have locked onto their location.
moves.note: Maxroll gives no damage type for the Turrets

moves.name: Melee
moves.avoid: can be tanked.
moves.maxrollQuote: Argentus uses a basic Melee Attack that does low Physical Damage that can be tanked.

moves.name: Ice Stab
moves.tell: stabs with his spear in a line in front of him
moves.avoid: Try to avoid Ice Stab by strafing as soon as you see the telegraph. It's a quick attack, so you may not be able to avoid all of them. Make sure to have good Cold Resistance just in case.
moves.maxrollQuote: Argentus stabs with his spear in a line in front of him. The attack does moderate Cold and Physical Damage, also applying Frostbite.

moves.name: Fire Bomb
moves.tell: creates a spiral of AoE circles that originate on him and explode outward
moves.avoid: You can easily dodge Fire Bomb by moving right on top of Argentus as soon as you see the telegraph.
moves.maxrollQuote: Argentus creates a spiral of AoE circles that originate on him and explode outward, doing moderate Fire Damage

moves.name: Ice Nova
moves.avoid: Move out of Ice Nova as soon as the telegraph begins. You have a short period of time before he begins to channel.
moves.maxrollQuote: Argentus channels a circular AoE around him that does high Cold Damage, Chills, and applies Frostbite.

moves.name: Flame Dash
moves.avoid: This attack is easily tanked.
moves.maxrollQuote: Argentus charges the player, doing low Fire and Physical Damage to players caught in his path. This attack is easily tanked.

moves.name: Flame Leap
moves.tell: Argentus leaps into the air and then comes crashing down / The skill is well telegraphed
moves.avoid: can be avoided by running outside of the circle and in between the columns.
moves.maxrollQuote: Argentus leaps into the air and then comes crashing down, doing Fire Damage in both a circular area around him and through three Impact Flares going outward. Does moderate/high damage with Flares doing more damage than the circle. This attack only occurs during Phase 3.

moves.name: Minions
moves.severity: LightMage Meteor high; overlapping meteors can be deadly
moves.tell: (circles of light on the ground)
moves.avoid: avoid Lightmage's Meteor attack at all costs (circles of light on the ground). Prioritize killing Lightmage's so that they don't overwhelm you with Meteors.
moves.maxrollQuote: During phase 2 Argentus leaves the arena and a number of Osprix LightMages, Vanguards, and Raiders spawn that must be killed. Vanguards and Raiders aren't particularly dangerous, but LightMages have a Meteor attack that does high Fire Damage and multiple LightMages often overlap their Meteors. Getting hit by multiple Meteors can be deadly.
moves.note: Fire is the Osprix LightMage Meteor; Vanguards and Raiders have no stated element

tips: In phase 2, LightMage Meteors show as circles of light and overlapping meteors can be deadly. Kill the LightMages first and stay out of the circles.
Ice Nova deals high Cold damage after a short telegraph. Leave the circle as soon as it starts, and bring capped Cold and Fire resistance.
In phase 3, Flame Leap adds Fire flares. Run outside the circle and between the columns.
strategy: Phase 1: In Phase 1 you fight Argentus alone. This is a fairly straightforward phase where you burn down Argentus.

Phase 2: At 50% health Argentus flies out of the arena and Osprix LightMages, Vanguards, and Raiders begin to spawn. All of them must be killed before you can move on to Phase 3.... Turrets continue to fire during this Phase so avoid them.
Phase 3: The last phase is similar to the first one with the only difference being Argentus now uses Flame Leap along with his other skills.
Maxroll guide line: Argentus is a relatively easy fight but does have some mechanics that need to be avoided.
god-hunter-argentus.resist: This fight is mostly Fire and Cold damage so make sure to have those Resistances capped.

page.title: Harton’s Husk – Fall of the Empire Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Oblivion Spike
moves.tell: Harton fires out two lines in front of him
moves.avoid: Don't stand in Oblivion Spike - It deals more damage over the skill's duration which gives you time to move out after Harton casts it, but if you wait too long it becomes painful quickly.
moves.maxrollQuote: Harton fires out two lines in front of him that do Void Damage Over Time. The Damage of this skill increases each second.

moves.name: Abyssal Sundering
moves.maxrollQuote: When Harton reaches 65% HP he uses this skill in conjunction with Oblivion Spike. This skill adds additional spikes to the area that do low Void Hit and DoT damage but get stronger over time.

moves.name: Idols of Ruin
moves.avoid: Avoid Barrage of Ruin from the Idols of Ruin - Like Oblivion Spike its damage increases over the duration of the skill. / Don't kill the Idols of Ruin - While killing them removes several mechanics, they have almost as much HP as Harton. Focusing on them just prolongs the fight instead of making it easier.
moves.maxrollQuote: These are two large worms that are similar to the Idol of Loathing found in Act 1 of the campaign but with an additional skill. They persist throughout the fight unless killed and have almost as much HP as Harton. They have three skills: Bite is a Melee Attack that does low Physical Damage, Death Seeker is a line attack that targets the player and does low Void Damage and Barrage of Ruin is a channeled AoE DoT that does low Void Damage but gets stronger every second.

moves.name: Claw Slam
moves.maxrollQuote: Harton slams the ground in front of him, doing moderate Physical Damage.

moves.name: Corrupted Slash
moves.maxrollQuote: Harton swings in Melee Range in front of him, doing low Physical and Void Damage.

moves.name: Void Stab
moves.maxrollQuote: Harton stabs in front of him with a circular AoE Hit that does moderate Void Damage.

tips: Oblivion Spike and Barrage of Ruin gain damage every second. Step out right away instead of finishing your attack.
Most of his hits are low damage but they overlap. Keep moving and cap Void and Physical resistance.
The Idols of Ruin have almost as much health as Harton, so Maxroll advises not killing them here. Note that Idols left alive carry into the Harbinger of Treason fight.
strategy: Single phase: Harton is a single phase fight. He has access to nearly all of his skills from the beginning and the ones he gains later on are not threatening, meaning this fight stays at about the same level of difficulty throughout.
Maxroll guide line: Keep moving - There's a lot going on, but most of it can be avoided simply by not standing still.
Maxroll guide line: The fight may seem overwhelming at first but the low damage output of most of the skills grants a lot of room for error, making this one of the easier Timeline boss fights.
hartons-husk.resist: Damage is mostly Void with some Physical so makes sure to cap both Resistances.

page.title: Heorot – The Age of Winter Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Frost Beam
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot fires a beam that deals low Cold Damage and Freezes. The damage increases over the duration of the beam.

moves.name: Frosted Eruption/Frozen Orb
moves.avoid: For the first quarter of the fight be ready to hide behind the pillars created by Frosted Eruption. The pillars block the shrapnel from Frozen Orb, which Heorot casts immediately after creating the pillars. Once he reaches 75% HP he no longer uses Frozen Orb.
moves.maxrollQuote: This is a combo skill. Heorot starts by placing several pillars that do moderate Cold Damage. If his health is above 75% he also fires a Frozen Orb that deals moderate Cold Damage with a high hit rate that also fires shrapnel. The shrapnel can be avoided by standing behind one of the pillars.

moves.name: Ice Stab
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot quickly stabs in front of him, doing moderate Cold and Physical Damage.

moves.name: Ice Spear
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot fires a spear at the player that deals low Cold Damage. He only uses this ability if the player is out of Melee Range.

moves.name: Ice Circle
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot explodes the ground around him three times in quick succession. Each explosion is larger, deals more damage and is farther away from Heorot than the last.

moves.name: Charge
moves.severity: While it deals no damage this skill can be deadly when combined with Blizzard.
moves.avoid: There are two strategies to deal with this: 1) have a movement ability ready, or 2) try to position Heorot so that he charges into a nearby wall.... Ultimately the best strategy is to try for 2 while being prepared to use your movement ability if it fails.
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot charges away from the player. He moves more than a screen away if he doesn't hit a wall. While it deals no damage this skill can be deadly when combined with Blizzard.
moves.note: Maxroll: "While it deals no damage"

moves.name: Blizzard
moves.tell: AT 75% HP Heorot casts Blizzard.
moves.avoid: While Blizzard is active only the space near Heorot is safe to stand in.
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot summons a large swirling Blizzard around him that deals Cold Damage and Shreds Cold Resistance. The damage increases each second you're in it, becoming deadly quickly. While Blizzard is active only the space near Heorot is safe to stand in.

moves.name: Jump Back
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot jumps back a short distance. Dangerous when combined with Blizzard.
moves.note: Maxroll lists no damage for Jump Back

moves.name: Ice Guard
moves.avoid: The first time he summons Grael and Spirit of Jormun, who must be killed to break Heorot's Ice Guard. The second time he summons Ice Wolves
moves.maxrollQuote: Heorot entombs himself in ice, becoming invulnerable. He uses this skill twice throughout the fight: at 55% and 35% health. The first time he summons Grael and Spirit of Jormun, who must be killed to break Heorot's Ice Guard. The second time he summons Ice Wolves and will continue summoning them after Ice Guard is broken and until Heorot is killed.

tips: After 75 percent, Blizzard keeps only the area near him safe and Shreds Cold resistance. If he charges away, use movement to get back next to him, or bait the charge into a wall.
In the first quarter, hide behind the Frosted Eruption pillars to block Frozen Orb shrapnel.
Frost Beam Freezes and ramps up. Sidestep it, and cap Cold and Physical resistance.
strategy: Single phase (with two immunity periods): Heorot is technically a single phase fight. He has two short periods of immunity with add spawns, but there are no arena changes and his overall skill set remains largely the same.
Ice Guard at 55% HP: For the first he only spawns two adds that need to be killed in order to break Heorot out of his Ice Guard.

Ice Guard at 35% HP: During the second he spawns a series of wolves. You need to kill several waves of wolves to break him out, but even after Heorot reengages the wolves will continue to spawn until the end of the fight.
Maxroll guide line: Heorot has two attack combos (Frosted Eruption with Frozen Orb and Charge with Blizzard) that are the cause of most of the deaths in this fight.

Maxroll guide line: This fight largely comes down to avoiding two mechanics. By using the pillars from Frosted Eruption to avoid Frozen Orb shards in the first quarter of the fight and staying out of Blizzard during the last 3 quarters the rest of the fight will be more than manageable.
heorot-monolith.resist: Damage is mostly Cold with some Physical so make sure to cap both Resistances.

page.title: Lagon – Ending The Storm Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Moon Beam
moves.severity: extremely high; deadly for almost every build
moves.tell: Lagon starts the attack by rising up and then repositions to either side of the player. / wait for Lagon's eye to glow red while he simultaneously rises up
moves.avoid: The best way to avoid this attack is to wait for Lagon's eye to glow red while he simultaneously rises up, then move to the opposite side of the platform.
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon rises up and then moves to either side of where the player was standing when he started. He then sweeps towards and across the player's original position with a beam that deals extremely high Cold and Lightning Damage at a high rate of fire and Chills. This attack is deadly for almost every build!

moves.name: Moon Shot
moves.tell: Lagon lowers his head and then fires a quick beam in front of him
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon lowers his head and then fires a quick beam in front of him, dealing moderate Cold and Lightning Damage. He only uses this skill when below 65% HP.

moves.name: Moon Blast
moves.severity: very high; one shots many builds
moves.tell: Lagon rises up and places a large circle on the ground below him.
moves.avoid: Do not get hit by Moon Blast. It's a well telegraphed attack with a big circle AoE so you shouldn't miss it.
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon rises up and places a large circle on the ground below him. After a short period he blasts the area with very high Cold and Lightning Damage and Slows. This attack one shots many builds!

moves.name: Lightning Strikes
moves.tell: A circular telegraph appears on the ground moments before the attack occurs.
moves.maxrollQuote: Lightning strikes random areas of the arena throughout the fight, dealing low Lightning Damage. A circular telegraph appears on the ground moments before the attack occurs.

moves.name: Melee Attacks
moves.avoid: Avoid his Melee Attacks, especially the left one (your right). It always stuns and could mess up your timing with more dangerous attacks.
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon strikes the ground in front of him with either his left or right claw, dealing moderate Physical Damage. His left claw (on your right side) is a guaranteed 2 second stun on hit.
moves.note: Maxroll: left claw (your right side) is a guaranteed 2 second stun on hit

moves.name: Tentacles
moves.avoid: They must be killed in order to progress to the next phase.
moves.maxrollQuote: During phase 2, Lagon's tentacles appear in the arena. They deal low damage Physical Attacks but have a high Stun Chance. You must kill these in order to progress to Phase 3.

moves.name: Adds
moves.avoid: not dealing with the Flayer Sharks causes them to accumulate and potentially overwhelm you.
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 2 Flayer Sharks and Crabs spawn throughout the phase. Neither are a major threat but the Flayer Sharks can get dangerous if too many are allowed to accumulate.

moves.name: Cold Waves
moves.avoid: They can be avoided in Phase 3 by hugging Lagon's side of the platform. / The easiest way to avoid them is to stand as close to Lagon's end of the platform as possible and slightly off center. The very center won't be far enough to avoid the waves but being too far off center puts you in danger of Moon Beam. / Make sure you have capped Cold Resistance in case you need to tank a few.
moves.maxrollQuote: Starting at Phase 2 and persisting into Phase 3, these waves do a moderate amount of Cold Damage and serve as a gear check for the fight. Builds with low Cold Resistance struggle to overcome these. They can be dodged but their spawn rate is so high in Phase 2 that avoiding them all is difficult. They can be avoided in Phase 3 by hugging Lagon's side of the platform.

tips: Moon Beam is deadly for almost every build. When he rises and his eye glows red, move to the opposite side of the platform.
Moon Blast marks a big circle under him and one shots many builds. Leave the circle before the blast lands.
His left claw (your right) always stuns. Stay out of his melee strikes, and in phase 3 hug his side of the platform slightly off center to avoid the Cold waves.
strategy: Phase 1: You start in the middle of the arena and need to run up the stairs on the left or right side to engage the boss. In the first phase Lagon has most of his abilities, including the most dangerous ones so you'll need to be on your toes from the start. Lagon is invulnerable. You must attack his tentacles to deal damage to him.

Phase 2: Once Lagon reaches 50% HP he teleports you to the center of the arena. This phase has entirely different mechanics from Phase 1.... The moon in the center of the ring fills up as you kill more Tentacles and once it's full you are teleported back to Lagon where Phase 3 starts.
Phase 3: This phase is similar to Phase 1 but the Cold Waves from Phase 2 now cross from the left and right side of the platform.

Maxroll guide line: There are several one shot mechanics in this fight, including one of the most punishing boss mechanics in the game, so knowing how to deal with these mechanics is vital to defeating this boss.
Maxroll guide line: Whatever you do, don't get hit by Moon Beam!
lagon-monolith.resist: Cap Lightning, Cold and Physical Resistances

page.title: Rahyeh – The Black Sun Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL

moves.name: Dive Bomb
moves.tell: Rahyeh launches into the air and crashes down at the target location... There's a short delay between when he launches into the air and when he crashes down that gives the player time to move away.
moves.avoid: Dive Bomb and Void Blast can be most easily avoided by running directly at Rahyeh where the distance to the edge of the attack is shortest.
moves.maxrollQuote: Rahyeh launches into the air and crashes down at the target location doing high Void Damage. There's a short delay between when he launches into the air and when he crashes down that gives the player time to move away.

moves.name: Void Blast
moves.tell: There's a short delay between when he targets the area and when the attack occurs which gives the player time to move away.
moves.avoid: Dive Bomb and Void Blast can be most easily avoided by running directly at Rahyeh where the distance to the edge of the attack is shortest.... Void Blast requires Rahyeh to be in Melee Range so you can prevent multiple uses of it by moving out of Melee Range until he uses another skill.
moves.maxrollQuote: Rahyeh slams a large area in front of him doing high Void Damage. There's a short delay between when he targets the area and when the attack occurs which gives the player time to move away.

moves.name: Void Flares
moves.tell: Rahyeh moves to the center of the arena and begins charging a series of conal attacks in a pie shaped pattern
moves.avoid: Every attack can be dodged by either shifting clockwise/counterclockwise or moving back and forth between two cones.
moves.maxrollQuote: Rahyeh moves to the center of the arena and begins charging a series of conal attacks in a pie shaped pattern that do high Void Damage. Every attack can be dodged by either shifting clockwise/counterclockwise or moving back and forth between two cones.

moves.name: Wave Dash
moves.tell: Rahyeh flies to just outside of the arena, then dashes through the arena to the other side.
moves.avoid: Avoid this attack by standing in place until Rahyeh dashes toward you, then move to either side of him. / Move out of this immediately and wait for it to dissipate before returning to that side of the arena.
moves.maxrollQuote: Rahyeh flies to just outside of the arena, then dashes through the arena to the other side. The dash leaves a trail in his wake that remains for several seconds and does high Void Dot Damage. Avoid this attack by standing in place until Rahyeh dashes toward you, then move to either side of him.

moves.name: Void Skyfall
moves.avoid: getting hit by multiple is costly and they can overlap. This means getting stunned by a meteor can be deadly, so make sure to avoid them.
moves.maxrollQuote: Rahyeh casts a series of meteor-like projectiles over several seconds. Each meteor does moderate Void Damage.

moves.name: Summon Adds
moves.avoid: they aren't threatening and can be killed quickly.
moves.maxrollQuote: Rahyeh fires a series of projectiles that turn into Voidform minions when they hit the ground. Voidforms are low damage and HP, they aren't threatening and can be killed quickly.

tips: Void Flares fire cones in a pie pattern. Rotate with the gaps or step back and forth between two cones.
The Wave Dash trail deals high Void damage over time. Wait until he commits, step to his side, and stay off that trail until it fades.
Dive Bomb and Void Blast hit high. Run toward him, where the edge of the area is closest, and bring capped Void resistance.
strategy: Single phase: Rahyeh is a single phase fight, with the tempo of the fight being determined by when he uses Void Flares and Wave Dash.... Rahyeh having access to all of his abilities from the beginning and maintaining them throughout.
Maxroll guide line: Void Flare has the highest learning curve. It requires an understanding of the pattern in order to dodge the attacks.
Maxroll guide line: His attacks can be punishing but they're all well telegraphed, making it possible for a skilled player to never take any damage from this fight.
rahyeh-the-black-sun.resist: This is a purely Void Damage fight, so make sure to have your Void Resistance capped.

page.title: The Husk of Elder Gaspar – The Last Ruin Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Tri-Beam Fire
moves.tell: Whenever Gaspar teleports to the center of the arena, get ready for Tri-Beam Fire.
moves.avoid: He always channels it in a counterclockwise rotation so be prepared to run in that direction. The rotation speed isn't very fast so a decent pair boots with Movement Speed should be enough to avoid the beams.
moves.maxrollQuote: Gaspar Teleports to the center of the arena and channels three beams that rotate counterclockwise. There is one beam for each element type ( Fire, Cold, Lightning ) with all of them dealing high damage that increases the longer the beams are active.
moves.note: Maxroll: beams rotate counterclockwise. The Harbinger of Fear page says walk clockwise for the Harbinger turret; direction unresolved between pages

moves.name: Frozen Ice Storm
moves.tell: He always uses this skill directly after Tri-Beam Fire.
moves.avoid: A build with adequate defenses and sustain can tank this attack. It can also be avoided by shuffling side to side as he rotates the attack back and forth.
moves.maxrollQuote: Gaspar launches a series of swirling Cold tornados outward from his body in an alternating pattern that deal moderate damage. He always uses this skill directly after Tri-Beam Fire.

moves.name: Teleport With Void Explosion
moves.maxrollQuote: Gaspar teleports to another location in the arena. Upon reaching his destination he sets off an explosion that does low Void Damage.

moves.name: Summon Flaming Void Totem
moves.avoid: Totems should be killed whenever possible to avoid accumulating too many. Once Gaspar reaches 60% HP he begins to drop twice as many Totems, so managing them becomes even more important.
moves.phase: Two totems per cast from 60% health
moves.maxrollQuote: Gaspar summons a totem that mimics his own Flame Burst, an ability that does high Fire Damage in a circle around the caster. When Gaspar reaches 60% health he summons two totems instead of one. Totems have relatively low health and can be killed.

moves.name: Spark Discharge
moves.avoid: There's a short delay between the initial touch and the explosion, so the blast can be completely avoided by players who have sufficient move speed or a movement ability. Try to detonate these during periods where you don't have to deal with other mechanics to keep them from piling up.
moves.maxrollQuote: Gaspar summons several balls of lightning that explode when touched, dealing moderate Lightning Damage.

moves.name: Doom Blast With Voidic Whirlwind
moves.tell: several large but well telegraphed explosions around the arena
moves.avoid: Doom Blast... should be avoided.... Voidic Whirlwind which increases in damage over its duration and should be avoided at all costs. The whirlwind only appears on the outskirts of the arena so stand near the center until it dissipates.
moves.maxrollQuote: Gaspar creates several large but well telegraphed explosions around the arena that do high Void Damage. Shortly after, a Whirlwind is formed on the outside of the arena that persists for several seconds and deals high Void Damage that increases over its duration.

tips: When he teleports to the center, Tri-Beam Fire follows. Its beams rotate counterclockwise, so move the same way and keep pace.
Doom Blast and the outer Voidic Whirlwind deal high Void damage. Avoid the marked explosions and stay near the center until the whirlwind ends.
Kill Flaming Void Totems and trigger Spark mines during quiet moments so they do not pile up. Cap Void, Fire, Cold and Lightning resistance.
strategy: Single phase: Gaspar is a 1 phase fight. He has access to all of his skills from the beginning so the difficulty of the fight is largely the same throughout.

Maxroll guide line: Gaspar has a number of skills that can be deadly, but fortunately they are all well telegraphed and easy to avoid on their own. The real danger is letting too many of his skills accumulate, leaving nowhere to go.

Maxroll guide line: The keys to successfully defeating Gaspar are 1) Familiarizing yourself with the cadence of Tri-Beam Fire and 2) managing the quantity of Flaming Void Totems and Sparks to prevent yourself from becoming overwhelmed.
husk-of-elder-gaspar.resist: The fight has high damage abilities that use Void, Fire, Cold and Lightning so you need to cap all four Resistances.

page.title: Lagon Chapter 8 Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Moon Beam
moves.severity: extremely high; one shots almost every build
moves.tell: Lagon rises up and moves to either side of you; his eye glows red
moves.avoid: Maxroll: wait for the red eye while he rises, then move to the opposite side of the platform
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon rises up and then moves to either side of where the player was standing when he started. He then sweeps towards and across the player's original position with a beam that deals extremely high Cold and Lightning Damage at a high rate of fire and Chills. This attack one shots almost every build!

moves.name: Moon Shot
moves.tell: lowers his head, then a quick beam in front
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon lowers his head and then fires a quick beam in front of him, dealing moderate Cold and Lightning Damage. He only uses this skill when below 65% HP.

moves.name: Moon Blast
moves.severity: very high; one shots many builds
moves.tell: rises and places a large circle under himself
moves.avoid: leave the circle before the blast
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon rises up and places a large circle on the ground below him. After a short period he blasts the area with very high Cold and Lightning Damage and Slows. This attack one shots many builds!

moves.name: Lightning Strikes
moves.tell: circular telegraph moments before the strike
moves.maxrollQuote: Lightning strikes random areas of the arena throughout the fight, dealing low Lightning Damage. A circular telegraph appears on the ground moments before the attack occurs.

moves.name: Melee Attacks
moves.avoid: Maxroll: avoid his melee, especially the left claw
moves.maxrollQuote: Lagon strikes the ground in front of him with either his left or right claw, dealing moderate Physical Damage. His left claw (on your right side) is a guaranteed 2 second stun on hit.
moves.note: left claw (your right side) is a guaranteed 2 second stun on hit

moves.name: Tentacles Phase
moves.maxrollQuote: During phase 2, Lagon's tentacles appear in the arena. They deal low damage Physical Attacks but have a high Stun Chance. You must kill these in order to progress to Phase 3.
moves.note: Maxroll gives high Stun Chance, not a guaranteed Stun; Stun not listed as an ailment

moves.name: Adds
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 2 Flayer Sharks and Crabs spawn throughout the phase. Neither are a major threat but the Flayer Sharks can get dangerous if too many are allowed to accumulate.
moves.note: Flayer Sharks and Crabs; no damage type stated

moves.name: Cold Waves
moves.avoid: Maxroll: hard to avoid all of them; cap Cold resistance in case you must tank some
moves.maxrollQuote: Starting at Phase 2, these waves do a moderate amount of Cold Damage and serve as a gear check for the fight. Builds with low Cold Resistance struggle to overcome these. They can be dodged but their spawn rate is so high avoiding them all is difficult.

tips: Moon Beam one shots almost every build. When he rises and his eye glows red, move to the opposite side of the platform.
Moon Blast drops a big circle under him. Leave it before the blast, since it one shots many builds.
Phase 2 Cold waves are hard to dodge while tentacles stun. Kill tentacles quickly and bring capped Cold resistance.
strategy: Phase 1: Lagon is invulnerable; attack his tentacles to damage him (Maxroll notes tentacles were added to phases 1 and 3 in 0.9.2).
Phase 2 at 50% HP: you are teleported to the center; kill tentacles to fill the moon while Flayer Sharks, Crabs and Cold Waves pressure you.
Phase 3: identical to phase 1 but Lagon is tankier.
lagon-campaign.summary: Maxroll: three phase fight with a guaranteed one shot mechanic and several others that one shot most builds.
lagon-campaign.resist: The fight is largely Cold and Lightning Damage, but also includes some Physical Damage so be sure to cap all three Resistances.

page.title: Lagon – Ending The Storm Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Lizard_IRL.

moves.name: Tentacle attack
moves.avoid: Maxroll: they must be killed to progress to phase 3
moves.maxrollQuote: During phase 2, Lagon's tentacles appear in the arena. They deal low damage Physical Attacks but have a high Stun Chance. You must kill these in order to progress to Phase 3.
moves.note: Same text on the campaign and monolith Lagon pages

tips: Tentacle hits are low Physical damage with a high stun chance. Kill nearby tentacles first so a stun does not leave you in a Cold wave.

page.title: Majasa Chapter 9 Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by Terek. Reviewed by Dredscythe, Mcfluffin.

moves.name: Stone Stare
moves.severity: at 4 stacks you turn to stone and cannot act
moves.avoid: Maxroll: avoid at all cost; cleanse remaining stacks
moves.maxrollQuote: Majasa periodically stares at you in both Phases, giving you stacks of Stone Stare. At 4 stacks, you turn to stone, unable to do anything. Avoid this ability in both Phases at all cost!
moves.note: Maxroll strategy calls the beam Flamethrower and says to cleanse Stone Stare stacks

moves.name: Siege Bolt
moves.severity: can one shot most builds at this point if it crits
moves.tell: giant red AoE
moves.avoid: Maxroll: avoid at all cost
moves.maxrollQuote: In Phase 1, Majasa cast a giant red AoE. If it crits, it can one shot most builds at this point in the game. Avoid this ability at all cost!
moves.note: Maxroll color-marks the red AoE as fire but states no damage type

moves.name: Fire and Poison Bolt
moves.tell: cast when you are too far from her
moves.avoid: Maxroll: step sideways; stay close so she does not cast ranged bolts
moves.maxrollQuote: In Phase 1, Majasa cast Poison or Fire Bolts when you are too far away from her. Dodge this ability by stepping sideways.

moves.name: Stalactite Falling
moves.tell: stalactites leave a Poison pool
moves.avoid: Maxroll: stand at the top or bottom of the arena where pools cannot spawn
moves.maxrollQuote: In Phase 1, Majasa cast Stalactite Falling that leaves a Poison pool for a while. You can avoid them entirely by positioning yourself at the top or bottom of the arena.
moves.note: Maxroll color-marks the name as poison and says it leaves a Poison pool; no hit element stated

moves.name: Stomp
moves.tell: big ice block with lightning sparks appears above your head; then lightning spikes launch toward you
moves.avoid: Maxroll: move in a circular motion
moves.maxrollQuote: In Phase 1, Majasa cast Stomp, a two step ability that deals high Lightning damage. It first targets you, then when it hits the ground, it launches lightning spikes towards you. To dodge both parts of the ability, move in a circular motion.

moves.name: Adds
moves.avoid: Maxroll: focus the Fire Essence first
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 1 at 66% and 33% Health, Majasa goes underground and summons 3 Essences, each with their own element. Focus the Fire one first.
moves.note: 3 Essences, each with its own element

tips: Siege Bolt shows a giant red area and a critical hit can one shot most builds at this stage. Leave the red area every time.
Stone Stare turns you to stone at 4 stacks. Avoid her stare and cleanse leftover stacks, for example with a potion cleanse affix.
Stand at the top or bottom of the arena near her. Pools cannot spawn there and she stops casting ranged bolts.
strategy: Phase 1: dodge her abilities; at 66% and 33% she goes underground and spawns 3 Essences; kill the Fire one first.
majasa-phase-1.summary: Maxroll: two phase fight, currently the hardest campaign boss and a defense check.
majasa-phase-1.resist: Phase 1 damage is diverse with Fire, Lightning and Poison while Phase 2 is only Physical. Cap all four (Physical highest priority). Maxroll also recommends at least 700 Health, a cleanse (Ward and Ailment Cleansing on Potion Use belt affix), at least 200 Armor, 200 dodge for rogues, endurance as a later priority, and enough recovery to refill health over 3 seconds.

page.title: Majasa Chapter 9 Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by Terek. Reviewed by Dredscythe, Mcfluffin.

moves.name: Melee attacks
moves.tell: she hunts you down
moves.avoid: Maxroll: hard to avoid, do not bother dodging; bring armor and recovery
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 2, Majasa goes berserk and starts chasing you. Her melee attacks apply Armor Shred and are hard to avoid, don't bother dodging them.
moves.note: Physical from Maxroll's phase statement "Phase 2 is only Physical"

moves.name: Tail Attack
moves.avoid: Maxroll: do not bother dodging
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 2, Majasa attacks with her tail. It also applies Armor Shred, but don't bother dodging it.
moves.note: Physical from the phase 2 statement

moves.name: Corrupting Bomb
moves.tell: she spits Blood Pools, then calls them back
moves.avoid: Maxroll: never stand in the Blood Pools (many Armour Shred stacks); move away when she calls them back
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 2, Majasa spits out Blood Pools at a regular interval, then after a set time, she calls the Blood Pools back to cast Corrupting Bomb. Never stand in the Blood Pools as it applies a ton of Armor Shred stacks!
moves.note: Physical from the phase 2 statement

moves.name: Regen
moves.tell: at 50% she rushes to a closed sarcophagus to heal to full, twice
moves.avoid: Maxroll: damage her freely during the heal
moves.maxrollQuote: During Phase 2, when Majasa gets to 50% Health, she opens one of the two sarcophagus to heal back to full. Take advantage of this window to damage her freely. Once both sarcophagus are open, she doesn't heal anymore.

tips: Phase 2 damage is Physical and her hits shred armor. Bring capped Physical resistance and recovery, since Maxroll says her melee is hard to avoid.
Never stand in her Blood Pools. They stack Armour Shred fast, and she later calls them back for Corrupting Bomb, so move away from her then.
Her stare carries into phase 2. Keep a cleanse ready for Stone Stare stacks.
strategy: Phase 2: at 0% she tears off part of herself and returns at full health; much more aggressive; heals to full at 50% twice using the sarcophagi; after both are used she cannot heal.
majasa-phase-2.resist: Phase 2 is only Physical; Maxroll prioritizes Physical resistance (75%).

page.title: Aberroth Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by Volca. Reviewed by LizardIRL.
page.changelog: [{"text": "Article created", "date": "2025-07-26T10:02:00"}, {"text": "Updated info on Frailty of Aberroth.", "date": "2025-09-11T01:20:18.685Z"}]

moves.name: Timeshattering Slam
moves.tell: Aberroth casts Absorbing Chaos to charge up for 4.5 seconds (3 seconds in Phase 5)
moves.avoid: Get in as much as damage as possible and move out before the attack goes off.
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth casts Absorbing Chaos to charge up for 4.5 seconds, then uses Timeshattering Slam to create a large increasing circle which deals massive Void and Physical damage.

moves.name: Persisting Void
moves.avoid: The pools have infinite duration but can be cleared with a Superheated Black Hole.
moves.maxrollQuote: Orbs that move from side to side. If you get hit by them, they leave behind Persisting Void which deals Void damage.

moves.name: Void Beam
moves.tell: Void Beams target you for 2.5 seconds and then fire at your location
moves.avoid: They persist between phases, so the longer the fight lasts, the more beams you'll have. Place them side-by-side: north and south of the arena are great places for them, leaving a lot of room for the final phase.
moves.maxrollQuote: Void Beams target you for 2.5 seconds and then fire at your location, dealing Void damage and applying Frailty of Aberroth.

moves.name: Superheated Black Hole
moves.tell: cast at your location after 1.5 seconds
moves.avoid: Use it to clear pools of Persisting Void from the ground.
moves.maxrollQuote: Superheated Black Hole is cast at your location after 1.5 seconds, dealing a small amount of Fire damage and applying Ignite.

moves.name: Superchilled Black Hole
moves.maxrollQuote: Superchilled Black Hole is cast at your location and deals moderate Cold damage. It also draws in Cold projectiles which deal a small amount of damage and apply Chill.

moves.name: Triple Flail Slam
moves.tell: Aberroth creates three triangles and then slams them one by one ... The boss first slams the area in the middle, then right and left (from the boss's perspective).
moves.avoid: The easiest way to handle this ability is by moving to the safe area behind the boss. You can also sidestep it by first standing in the left or right areas, then moving to the middle after the slam. Rogues can use Silver Shrouds to dodge it. With strong defenses, you can simply facetank it.
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth creates three triangles and then slams them one by one, dealing very high Void and Lightning damage.

moves.name: Slam + Ground of Destruction
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth slams the ground, dealing high Physical and Void damage. It creates Ground of Destruction in the same direction as the slam, which deals high Void damage over time.

moves.name: Called Meteors
moves.tell: Aberroth stays in place, calling multiple meteors towards him for 3 seconds.
moves.avoid: When the channeling begins, move to the side or behind the boss to avoid it.
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth stays in place, calling multiple meteors towards him for 3 seconds. The meteors deal high Fire damage and apply Ignite.

moves.name: Lobbed Meteors
moves.maxrollQuote: Medium-range lobbed meteor attack that deals high Cold damage and applies Frostbite.

moves.name: Roots
moves.avoid: Use movement abilities or a Cleanse to get out of it.
moves.maxrollQuote: Roots lock you in place for a short duration.

moves.name: Blade of Chaos
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth casts Blade of Chaos from its location, which travels in a wide arc. It deals moderate Physical, Lightning and Void damage.

moves.name: Cursing Scythe
moves.avoid: Avoid getting hit by it at all costs.
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth releases a total of 4 Necrotic bolts to deal damage and apply Curse of Aberroth, which reduces All Resistances by 10% and cannot be cleansed.
moves.note: ailments as stated: Curse of Aberroth (-10% All Resistances per stack, cannot be cleansed, unlimited stacks, duration 1,000,000 seconds)

moves.name: Cosmic Absorption / Lazer of Death
moves.tell: Aberroth charges up Cosmic Absorption for 2.5 seconds
moves.avoid: Move out of the charging area, then sidestep the Lazer.
moves.maxrollQuote: Aberroth charges up Cosmic Absorption for 2.5 seconds and then releases Lazer of Death for massive Void damage.

moves.name: Phase 3 quadrant ground effects (Quicksand / Lightning / Winds / Fiery Ground)
moves.avoid: The safest one to stand on is usually Fiery Ground, as long as you have enough sustain. It deals a small amount of Fire damage.
moves.maxrollQuote: Creates four quadrants, each with detrimental ground effects: Quicksand, Lightning, Winds and Fiery Ground.
moves.note: ailments as stated: Frailty of Aberroth (Quicksand); Shock of Aberroth: 5% increased damage taken per stack (Lightning); Chill of Aberroth: reduces movement, attack and cast speed (Winds)

moves.name: Regular attacks (Melee Attack, Charge, Flail Dash, Backward Hop)
moves.maxrollQuote: Regular attacks: Melee Attack, Charge, Flail Dash, Backward Hop

tips: Timeshattering Slam deals massive Void and Physical damage once Absorbing Chaos finishes charging. Leave the growing circle before it fires, sooner in the last phase.
Cursing Scythe applies Curse of Aberroth, minus 10 percent all resistances per stack, and it cannot be cleansed. Avoid its four Necrotic bolts above everything else.
In the last phase, Cosmic Absorption leads into Lazer of Death. Leave the charging area, then sidestep the beam, and park Void Beams side by side at north and south.
strategy: Phase 1 (100% - 77%): Aberroth gets access to new abilities in each phase. On phase transitions, it gains 90% less damage taken and stun immunity for 4.5 seconds.
Phase 2 (77% - 63%): In addition to previous abilities, it now uses Called Meteors, Lobbed Meteors and Roots. Uber Aberroth: A Harbinger spawns at the start of this phase.
Phase 3 (63% - 49%): Creates four quadrants, each with detrimental ground effects: Quicksand, Lightning, Winds and Fiery Ground.
Phase 4 (49% - 35%): Uses Cursing Scythe which applies Curse of Aberroth. Avoid getting hit by it at all costs. Uber Aberroth: A Harbinger spawns at the start of this phase.

Phase 5 (35% - 0%): Uses Cosmic Absorption to charge up for 2.5 seconds and then deal massive damage with Lazer of Death... Absorbing Chaos has a duration of 3 seconds instead of 4.5 seconds, which makes Timeshattering Slam happen faster. The boss arena is much smaller in this phase, making positioning even more important. Uber Aberroth: Heals to full health at the start of this phase.

location: Requires progressing through the Forgotten Knights questline and slaying all 10 Harbingers. Spend one Harbinger Eye at the Altar of Oblivion near the back of the Shattered Road to open a portal to face Aberroth.
Maxroll guide line: Keep the boss arena clean by clearing pools of Persisting Void with Superheated Black Hole.
Maxroll guide line: Place Void Beams correctly to get through the final phase.
Maxroll guide line: Build strong defenses against Void and Physical damage to survive the encounter.

Maxroll guide line: Frailty of Aberroth: 5% less damage per stack. 10% less health leech, ward retention, and health regen per stack. 50% reduced healing effectiveness per stack. Unlimited stacks, duration 4 seconds. Inflicted by multiple abilities, but Void Beams and Quicksand apply most of it.
aberroth.resist: Build strong defenses against Void and Physical damage to survive the encounter.

Uber difference: Void Beams apply a beam to both sides. Since the fight lasts much longer, placing Void Beams correctly is necessary to get through the final phase.
Uber difference: A Harbinger spawns at Phase 2 and Phase 4, making the boss immune until you defeat it.
Uber difference: Aberroth heals to full health at the start of Phase 5.

page.title: Vision of the Observer Boss Guide
page.byline: Written by Volca. Reviewed by BinaQc.

moves.name: Void Rift
moves.tell: The segments are always created in a clockwise pattern.
moves.maxrollQuote: Creates segments on the battlefield one after another, dealing very high Void damage.

moves.name: Persisting Void
moves.avoid: Stack the pools on top of each other to avoid filling the boss arena with them.
moves.maxrollQuote: Orbs that move towards the player, creating a damaging pool on hit. The damage type changes based on the active Omen.

moves.name: Void Meteor
moves.tell: The meteors are telegraphed with a shadowy line before they appear.
moves.maxrollQuote: Three meteors sweep the area, dealing high Void and Physical damage.

moves.name: Void Reform
moves.avoid: Move out of this skill's area at the end of its cast.
moves.maxrollQuote: Vision of the Observer teleports to the player's location, dealing moderate Void damage.

moves.name: Teleport
moves.maxrollQuote: Vision of the Observer teleports around the arena multiple times.

moves.name: Void Beam
moves.maxrollQuote: Vision of the Observer casts three beams from its location, dealing moderate Void damage over time.

moves.name: Frozen Ice Storm
moves.maxrollQuote: Slowly moving and expanding Cold area projectile.

moves.name: Orbiting Comet
moves.maxrollQuote: Projectiles orbit the outer edge of the arena, dealing high Cold damage.

moves.name: Flamethrower
moves.maxrollQuote: Vision of the Observer creates a cone of moderate Fire damage from its location.

moves.name: Starburst
moves.tell: Circle that explodes after a duration
moves.maxrollQuote: Circle that explodes after a duration, dealing high Fire damage.

moves.name: Falling Meteor
moves.avoid: Avoid standing near them at any cost.
moves.maxrollQuote: Three meteors stay on the ground for a short duration, dealing extremely high Physical and Void damage. Only used in the final phase.

moves.name: Ground of Destruction
moves.maxrollQuote: Lines on the ground that deal low Void damage over time for a long duration before disappearing. Only used in the final phase.

moves.name: Absorbing Meteors
moves.maxrollQuote: Three meteors fall from the sky, repeating multiple times in a sequence. They deal low Void damage. Only used in the final phase.

tips: Void Meteor and the final phase Falling Meteors deal very high Physical and Void damage. Watch for the shadowy line and never stand near landed meteors.
Most hits stack All Resistances Reduction, 5 percent per stack for 8 seconds. Avoid chip damage and cleanse when stacks build up.
Each Omen adds its element in order: Lightning, Void, Cold, then Fire. Stack Persisting Void pools together so the arena stays open.
strategy: Omen phases (Ward breakpoints at 80%, 60%, 40% and 20%): The fight against Vision of the Observer includes four different Omens that must be defeated one by one. Vision of the Observer and Omens are never vulnerable at the same time. The Omens appear in the following order: Omen of Havoc - Lightning; Omen of Silence - Void; Omen of Solitude - Cold; Omen of Strife - Fire. Vision of the Observer is damageable until it reaches its Ward breakpoints at 80%, 60%, 40% and 20% of its maximum Health. Each time a breakpoint is reached, the boss gains Invulnerability until an Omen is defeated. Vision of the Observer heals to full health after the final Omen is killed.
Final phase (None): Falling Meteor, Ground of Destruction and Absorbing Meteors are 'Only used in the final phase.'
location: Clear all three Omen encounters at once in Omen's Veil to get the Fractured Prison Woven Echo, then place it in your Echo Web at 400+ Corruption to fight Vision of the Observer.
Maxroll guide line: Many abilities of Vision of the Observer are similar to Shade of Orobyss and Aberroth.

Maxroll guide line: The boss mainly deals Void damage, and some of its abilities change their damage type to Lightning, Void, Cold and Fire depending on the current phase. It gains new abilities in each phase, with damage types matching the type of the active Omen.

Maxroll guide line: Vision of the Observer inflicts a negative Ailment, All Resistances Reduction, with most of its abilities. Each stack of it reduces All Resistances by 5% for 8 seconds. It has unlimited stacks, and it can be cleansed.
Maxroll guide line: Build strong defenses especially against Void damage to survive the encounter.

page.byline: Written by McFluffin. Reviewed by Facefoot, Lizard_IRL, Raxxanterax.

moves.name: Catastrophic Implosion
moves.severity: The Implosion kills most players with appropriate builds for the content, and one shots almost all builds at tier 4, so don't get caught in it!
moves.tell: Julra sets a huge clock in motion that, when it reaches 12 o'clock, causes a screen wide Void Damage AoE blast
moves.avoid: This attack can be avoided by switching Eras before the implosion occurs. ... make sure to use Temporal Shift before the clock strikes 12. ... If you happen to get caught and survive, you should immediately cleanse the Doom stacks that were applied to you.
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra sets a huge clock in motion that, when it reaches 12 o'clock, causes a screen wide Void Damage AoE blast that also applies 4 stacks of Doom.

moves.name: Dimension Tear
moves.tell: She always uses this ability a few seconds after teleporting to a new Timeline.
moves.avoid: It takes a short while for the puddle to form, and follows you until it finishes. Use this time to position the puddle to the edges of the room. ... Once the puddle is created, immediately run out (or use a movement skill if you have one). (Note: If you time it correctly, you can use Temporal Shift right before Catastrophic Implosion, then immediately use Temporal Shift to avoid creating a Dimension Tear).
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra leaves an AoE circle on the ground at the player's feet that lasts a long time and does high Void DoT Damage.

moves.name: Summon Pillars (Lightning Bolt)
moves.tell: In the Ruined Era, they become invulnerable and use Lightning Bolt, a telegraphed attack
moves.avoid: If Julra uses Summon Pillars while in the Divine Era, kill these as soon as you can. If you're in the Ruined Era, you have to dodge the attacks until you switch eras.
moves.maxrollQuote: Three pillars are created that exist in both eras, but work differently in each. In the Divine Era, they have no attacks and can be destroyed. In the Ruined Era, they become invulnerable and use Lightning Bolt, a telegraphed attack that does Lightning Damage and Shocks.

moves.name: Summon Healing Fountain
moves.avoid: Destroy any Healing Fountains as soon as you can to limit the healing they provide, but don't risk standing in damaging attacks to do so.
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra creates a fountain that heals her with projectiles that have a high rate of fire. Can be destroyed.

moves.name: Frigid Tide
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra casts a conal attack towards the player that does moderate Hit Cold Damage and Chills.

moves.name: Unraveling Decay
moves.tell: Four beams fire outward from the center of the arena that rotate clockwise.
moves.avoid: There is a sizable gap in each near the center that the player can stand in to avoid the attacks. ... This can be a particularly tough part of the fight for Melee Leech builds because Julra can stand in her own beams out of reach of the character, preventing Leech, so make sure to save some potions for this part of the fight.
moves.maxrollQuote: Four beams fire outward from the center of the arena that rotate clockwise. ... Getting hit does high Void Damage and Shreds Void Resistance.

moves.name: Temporal Shot
moves.avoid: Generally the best strategy is to keep moving to naturally dodge some of the mechanics ... some (Temporal Shot, Lightning Bolt from Summon Pillars) happen quickly, making them difficult to time.
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra fires a single, high speed projectile at the player that does moderate Void Damage.

moves.name: Chilled Seeker
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra fires a group of three projectiles at the player that will follow the player. Does low/moderate Hit Cold Damage.

moves.name: Shocking Impact
moves.tell: Julra fires a mortar-like attack that explodes in a circle on the ground.
moves.maxrollQuote: Julra fires a mortar-like attack that explodes in a circle on the ground. There's a small and large version of the attack, with both doing Lightning Damage but the larger one doing it in a larger area and for increased damage.

tips: Catastrophic Implosion is a screen wide Void blast with 4 Doom stacks when the clock reaches 12. Use Temporal Shift before then, and cleanse Doom if a hit lands.
Every shift makes Julra cast Dimension Tear under you. Lead the puddle to the room edge before it forms, step out, and shift only when needed.
During Unraveling Decay, stand in the gap near the center between the beams. They deal high Void damage and shred Void resistance.
strategy: phases note quote: The fight is chaotic, with no clear phases or other structured segments, and no clear pattern to many of the skills that she uses.

dungeon mechanic quote: Temporal Shift is a Dungeon specific ability that allows the player to switch between the Divine Era and Ruined Era Timelines at will (default button is 'D')... This can also be used to avoid boss mechanics.

location: Temporal Sanctum dungeon (Ruined Era); requires a Temporal Sanctum Key. Start in the Shining Cove in the Imperial Era. From the Portal head northeast until you see a large stone door. Open the door and head through the Portal to the Ruined Coast ... Pull the lever, and kill Ortra'ek the Survivor. The door to the east of you will open, and you can now enter the Temporal Sanctum.
Maxroll guide line: Julra is a more difficult fight than most of the other bosses in the game, so understanding the mechanics is pivotal to your success.
Maxroll guide line: Most of Julra's abilities are available to her at any given time, so you have to be prepared for all of them.

Maxroll guide line: You may be tempted to switch eras immediately, but doing so causes Julra to use another Dimension Tear. If you switch eras too often, these begin to pile up and could become overwhelming, so switch eras only when you need to.

Maxroll guide line: Prioritize the mechanics of the fight over dealing damage. While it can be tempting to try and burn Julra down to avoid too many puddles from Dimension Tear, a poorly placed puddle is far more difficult to deal with than a lot of well placed ones.

Maxroll guide line: Properly time your uses of Temporal Shift to avoid Catastrophic Implosion, consistently place the puddles from Dimension Tear, avoid the beams from Unraveling Decay and stay moving to avoid Julra's other attacks to successfully complete this boss, even on tier 4.

location: Lightless Arbor dungeon (Ruined Era); requires a Lightless Arbor Key. Start at The Surface waypoint and head to the entrance to the north that leads to The Shrouded Ridge. Upon arriving in The Shrouded Ridge head directly north until you reach the entrance to the Lightless Arbor.

Maxroll guide line: All of the other abilities are either very well telegraphed and easy to avoid or deal low enough damage to not be especially threatening on their own. Avoiding Spore Beam and Energy Wave are the most important parts of this phase.
Maxroll guide line: Understanding how the Pyres work and then avoiding Shockwave, Spore Beam and Energy Wave are the keys to your success.

moves.name: Fire & Necrotic Floor
moves.severity: The floor does high damage and will kill almost every build at tier 4.
moves.tell: He activates more sections as you deal damage and eventually the entire floor is activated.
moves.avoid: Once the entire floor is covered in the damaging effect be ready to switch immunities quickly.
moves.maxrollQuote: Cremorus activates parts of the floor, causing them to do high Necrotic Damage over Time. He activates more sections as you deal damage and eventually the entire floor is activated. At this point he begins switching the floor between Necrotic and Fire Damage.

moves.name: Flaming & Necrotic Orbiter
moves.maxrollQuote: Two types of skulls orbit Cremorus with one dealing moderate Necrotic and the other moderate Fire damage.

moves.name: Chaotic Soul
moves.maxrollQuote: A large skull is cast by Cremorus and chases the player, dealing low Fire and Necrotic damage.

moves.name: Incendiary Torrent
moves.tell: Cremorus channels a line of Fire at the position the player was standing when he firsts starts the channel.
moves.avoid: Avoid Incendiary Torrent. Even if you're Fire immune the Ignites can quickly kill a player who's switching during a ground transition.
moves.maxrollQuote: Cremorus channels a line of Fire at the position the player was standing when he firsts starts the channel. The wall does Fire Damage that increases every second and applies Ignite at a high frequency.

moves.name: Wall of Fire
moves.avoid: Wall of Fire and Collapsing Decay can both be avoided with a movement skill that has an invincibility frame (i.e. Teleport, Shift with Shadowslip, Transplant, Lunge with Unstoppable and Paranoia).
moves.maxrollQuote: A wall of Fire travels across the arena, dealing moderate Fire Damage.

moves.name: Raging & Vengeful Soul
moves.maxrollQuote: Cremorus casts a series of skull projectiles that alternate between Fire and Necrotic. Both deal moderate/high damage while Fire skulls apply Ignite and Necrotic skulls apply Marked for Death.
moves.note: ailments as stated: Ignite (Fire skulls); Marked for Death (Necrotic skulls)

moves.name: Summon Thrall & Golem Burst
moves.avoid: When Cremorus summons a Thrall run from it until it explodes.
moves.maxrollQuote: Cremorus summons a Thrall that chases the player and eventually creates a large burst that deals high Necrotic Damage and applies Marked for Death.

moves.name: Disintegration
moves.avoid: Avoid Disintegration. It does a lot of damage and also applies Marked for Death which increases the damage you take from all sources.
moves.maxrollQuote: Cremorus fires two projectiles that deal high Necrotic Damage in a large circle and apply Marked for Death.

moves.name: Collapsing Decay
moves.avoid: This attack cannot be dodged. ... Wall of Fire and Collapsing Decay can both be avoided with a movement skill that has an invincibility frame (i.e. Teleport, Shift with Shadowslip, Transplant, Lunge with Unstoppable and Paranoia).
moves.maxrollQuote: A Necrotic circle collapses into Cremorus that deals moderate Necrotic Damage. This attack cannot be dodged.

moves.name: Summon Skeletons
moves.maxrollQuote: 8 Imperial Guards are summoned that use Melee attacks and deal low Physical Damage.

tips: Once the whole floor is active, switch Soulfire Shield immunity quickly. Maxroll says the floor kills almost every build at tier 4.
Check for Ignite before switching from Fire to Necrotic immunity and cleanse it. Incendiary Torrent applies Ignite fast even if you are Fire immune.
Disintegration and the Thrall's Golem Burst apply Marked for Death. Avoid Disintegration and run from the Thrall until it bursts.
strategy: phases note quote: Cremorus is a single phase fight that gets progressively more difficult due to the floor becoming increasingly covered in a damaging effect that switches between Necrotic and Fire, eventually covering the entire floor and forcing players to use their immunity to avoid damage.

dungeon mechanic quote: Soulfire Shield is a Dungeon specific ability that allows the player to switch between Fire and Necrotic immunity. ... This can also be used to avoid boss mechanics since Cremorus is also themed around the same two damage types. Using Soulfire Shield costs Souls which are acquired by killing enemies

location: Soulfire Bastion dungeon (Imperial Era); requires a Soulfire Bastion Key. Start at the Risen Lake waypoint. From the waypoint head west then east at the crossroads. That will lead you to an entrance for The Felled Wood. Upon entering The Felled Wood head Northeast over a bridge until you arrive at the entrance to Soulfire Bastion. Do not take the door directly east as it leads to a different area.
Maxroll guide line: Cremorus has a full complement of skills that are generally broken up between fire and necrotic damage, which allows players to take advantage of the Soulfire Shield ability.

Maxroll guide line: This also creates scenarios where Cremorus uses an ability of the opposite damage type to the floor that is impossible to avoid for some builds, forcing those builds to tank the damage. For tier 3 and below this shouldn't be a problem as most builds can find enough defenses to mitigate the damage.

Maxroll guide line: For tier 4 we recommend using builds with: A movement ability that has an invincibility frame (i.e. Teleport, Shift with Shadowslip, Transplant, Lunge with Unstoppable and Paranoia). Sentinels can also use Rebuke to tank the damage. A Cleanse to deal with DoTs while switching. You can get this from either the Ward and Ailment Cleansing on Potion Use affix or skills like Shift with Molting.
Maxroll guide line: When switching immunities keep track of debuffs and cleanse if necessary. Switching from Fire to Necrotic while being Ignited can be deadly.
Maxroll guide line: Mastering the floor transition and keeping track of Ignites when switching from Fire to Necrotic immunity is the most difficult part of this fight.
